purpose: Phase 2b v3: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (Holm-corrected across encoders) turning v2's by-eye 4-median comparison into a proper paired test. Central claim: the label-free learned beta-NLL stochastic decoder beats the label-using matched_noise_per_type control (and the global matched_noise control) on energy distance and |log2 r_var| per-group variance-calibration error.
builds_on: phase2b_v2_results.json (same seeds/config); this run regenerated the uncached predictions and passed a 1e-6 reproducibility gate against the v2 medians.

energy_distance__stochastic_vs_matched_n.direction: lower is better (both metrics); negative median diff and win_fraction>0.5 => learned decoder better

r_var_abs_log2__stochastic_vs_matched_no.direction: lower is better (both metrics); negative median diff and win_fraction>0.5 => learned decoder better

metrics.energy_distance: proper distributional divergence (=0 iff equal); lower is better; the load-bearing discriminator.

notes.wilcoxon: two-sided, zero_method='wilcox'; paired across shared (dataset x cell type) groups.
notes.holm: Holm-Bonferroni step-down across the 4 encoders within each (metric, control) family.
notes.win_fraction: fraction of shared groups where the learned decoder's metric is strictly lower (better) than the control's.
notes.auxiliary_metrics_that_FAILED_to_discrim: correlation_attenuation and covariance_preservation, the two metrics proposed as 'independent noise cannot fake this', both failed as clean discriminators. cov_preservation is scale-invariant (independent noise attenuates all correlations by a common factor, preserving rank order). correlation_attenuation is monotone in the amount of injected noise in this regime (every value > 1; deterministic is over-correlated, any noise pulls it down toward 1, nothing overshoots below 1), so it measures how much you diluted, not whether the dilution was structured -- which is why the label-informed control 'wins' it. energy_distance is the metric that actually discriminates.
notes.r_var_dispersion_confound: r_var_dispersion is confounded by magnitude and must never be quoted alone: a near-zero-variance predictor (deterministic, r_var median ~0.12-0.26) gets the LOWEST dispersion of all. Restrict the dispersion comparison to variance-restoring variants (r_var median in [0.8,1.25]) and exclude deterministic.
